test.name: Collection mismatch: a high-scoring hit from the wrong decade is not an answer
test.description: The user asks for an 1870 census search; the index returns one result — a genuine Patrick Flynn scoring 0.94 at confidence 5/5 — from the 1850 collection. The match is real; the record is twenty years too early and answers nothing about young adulthood. Tests whether the skill overrides a very confident score on the collection title: log outcome 'partial' (not 'positive', which would mark 1870 as covered and hide the gap from research-exhaustiveness; not 'negative', since results did come back), write the sidecar (results were returned — the mirror of the nil rule, and research_append rejects an assertions append against a sidecar-less entry), name the returned collection in notes so a later reader can see why it was partial, and STOP rather than trying surname variants — the name indexed fine, so spelling was never the problem and variants cannot conjure an 1870 record the index does not hold. Note this is an ad-hoc search: no plan item covers 1870, the user asked for it directly, so per Step 1 it executes and per Step 8 it must not escalate to external sites.

input.user_message: Search the 1870 census for Patrick Flynn in Schuylkill County to see if he stayed in the area through young adulthood.

judge_context: record_search ranks host-side when it is called with projectPath AND subjectId, returning the ranking inline as `ranked` (match score + attachment flag for every candidate). The skill should pass subjectId and triage from `ranked` — NOT per-result same_person, NOT a separate source_attachments call, and NOT a separate rank_search_matches call (the search folds all three in).

The returned match is a genuine person match to Patrick Flynn (I1) and the inline ranking scores it high (matchScore ~0.94) — but it comes from collectionTitle='United States Census, 1850', which is a collection-mismatch for the 1870 search. A high person-match score does NOT override the collection sanity-check: the skill must NOT treat this 1850 result as the 1870 answer.

When the collection mismatches: (a) WRITE the sidecar (results were returned — omitting the sidecar is an error), (b) log outcome='partial' (NOT 'negative' — negative means zero results; partial means results found but not for the intended collection), (c) explain the mismatch in notes.

Collection-mismatch is NOT nil. After getting the wrong collection, the skill MAY attempt ONE retry with an explicit collectionId filter — this is correct genealogy practice. What is NOT acceptable: escalating to name-variant searches (Flinn, Flyn) after a mismatch, either during execution or as recommended next steps.

Result triage for collection-mismatch: when the returned collection year is obviously wrong (1850 returned for a 1870 search), the mismatch itself is sufficient to categorize the result as non-applicable — the review-surface triage should flag it via the collection sanity-check even though the ranking scored it high on the person. The skill need NOT run any additional same_person or source_attachments call (record_search already folded those in); the collection title alone establishes non-relevance for the 1870 question. Score Result triage=3 if the mismatch is identified and the result is correctly treated as non-applicable.

If the skill attempts or recommends variant surname searches (Flinn, Flyn, etc.) after identifying the collection mismatch, score Nil escalation=2 (partial misunderstanding). Recommending Ancestry or a different source as next steps is correct and should NOT be penalized.
If the collectionId retry also returns mismatched results, the skill should log both attempts as outcome='partial' and stop — no further searches needed.

Tool Arguments: score 3 if record_search was called with projectPath AND subjectId (subjectId is what triggers host-side ranking) plus appropriate search parameters. A validate_research_schema call with a project path after writing is acceptable and expected — do not penalize it. Only score 2 if record_search had clearly wrong arguments, or omitted subjectId when the research subject is known. Do NOT expect a separate rank_search_matches call — ranking is part of record_search now.

The core pass criteria: (1) outcome='partial' (not 'negative') for the 1850 mismatch, (2) sidecar written, (3) mismatch explained in notes, (4) NO variant surname searches executed after the mismatch, (5) next-step suggestions point to a different source or collection filter (not to Flinn/Flyn variants).

IMPORTANT — How file writes work: `research_log_append` writes the log entry AND the results/ sidecar host-side from the staged handle; the skill does not hand-write either. Sidecars are newly created files, so they never appear in the file-change diff — their absence from it is not evidence of anything.
